title: Workbench.jl
text: Workbench provides a development workspace manager for Julia packages. It scaffolds and manages sub-projects (test/, docs/, benchmark/, dev/, and custom task directories) as workspace members that share a single Manifest.toml with your package.

title: Installation
text: Install Workbench in your global environment — it is a developer tool, not a package dependency: julia> using Pkg; Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/mthelm85/Workbench.jl") Workbench requires Julia 1.12+ (workspace support).

title: Quick start
text:
From the root of your package: julia> using Workbench

julia> Workbench.init(:dev)                    # scaffold dev/ with startup.jl

julia> Workbench.add(:dev, "Infiltrator")      # add a dev dependency

julia> Workbench.activate(:dev)                # make dev deps available

julia> …

title: How it works
text: Julia 1.12 introduced workspaces — a mechanism for multiple sub-projects to share a single Manifest.toml. Workbench automates the creation and management of these workspace sub-projects.

title: LOAD_PATH stacking
text:
The key feature of activate is that it pushes the sub-project onto LOAD_PATH without changing the active Pkg project: julia> Workbench.activate(:dev)
julia> using Infiltrator           # resolves from dev/
julia> Pkg.add("NewDep")           # still targets the root package This is different from …

title: Subprocess isolation
text: run spawns a fresh Julia process with --project=<subdir> --startup-file=no, giving a clean isolation boundary. The subprocess isn't contaminated by whatever the developer has loaded in their REPL. This is particularly important for benchmarks, where stray loaded code can affect results.

title: Global startup hook
text:
To auto-activate :dev whenever you start Julia inside a package: # ~/.julia/config/startup.jl
try
    using Workbench
catch
    # Workbench not installed — skip
end
if @isdefined(Workbench)
    Workbench.activate(:dev; quiet=true)
end quiet=true silently returns nothing when there's no package …

title: Error handling
text: All Workbench-specific errors throw WorkbenchError, so you can distinguish them from unrelated failures. Invalid arguments (e.g. calling add with no package names) throw ArgumentError.

title: Workbench.WorkbenchError
text:
WorkbenchError <: Exception Thrown for all Workbench-specific failures: missing project roots, missing sub-project directories, TOML issues, subprocess failures, etc. Catch this type to distinguish Workbench problems from unrelated exceptions: try
    Workbench.activate(:dev)
catch e
    e isa …

title: Workbench.add
text:
add(name::Symbol, pkgs...; root=find_project_root()) Add packages to a sub-project's dependencies. Examples Workbench.add(:dev, "KaimonGate")
Workbench.add(:benchmark, "BenchmarkTools", "Statistics")

title: Workbench.rm
text: rm(name::Symbol, pkgs...; root=find_project_root()) Remove packages from a sub-project's dependencies. Examples Workbench.rm(:dev, "KaimonGate")

title: Workbench.activate
text: activate(name::Symbol; root=find_project_root(), quiet=false, force=false) Make a sub-project's dependencies available in the current REPL session by pushing its environment onto LOAD_PATH. If a startup.jl (for :dev) exists, it is executed afterward — in Main, so using X resolves via the stacked …

title: Workbench.deactivate
text:
deactivate(name::Symbol)
deactivate() Remove a sub-project from LOAD_PATH. With no arguments, deactivates all.

title: Workbench.example
text:
example(name::AbstractString; root=find_project_root(), args=``) Run an example script from the examples/ directory with the root project active. Examples are not workspace members — they use the parent package directly. Examples Workbench.example("basic")
Workbench.example("advanced")

title: Workbench.status
text: status(; root=find_project_root(), io=stdout) Display all discovered sub-projects, their state, and available actions. title: Workbench.find_project_root
text: find_project_root(start=pwd()) -> String Walk up from start looking for a Project.toml that has both name and uuid fields (i.e. a real package, not a sub-project or environment). Throws WorkbenchError if no package root is found.
